name: How can I tell whether the wall I want removed is load bearing?

mainEntity.name: How can I tell whether the wall I want removed is load bearing?

acceptedAnswer.text: A wall should not be removed until its structural role has been established by qualified project professionals. If it carries floor, roof, or upper-level loads, the solution may require a properly sized beam, posts, connection details, and adequate support below; local plan requirements can include structural documentation. Context: Even a non-load-bearing wall may conceal wiring, plumbing, ductwork, or ventilation that must be safely rerouted. Guessing from wall thickness or attic visibility is unreliable. Key factors: framing direction; supports above and below; foundation conditions; utilities. Practical guidance: Provide any old plans, renovation records, attic or crawlspace photos, and information about additions. Do not begin demolition based only on a visual assumption. Elite Remodeling & Design can include existing-condition review and design coordination before construction planning.
acceptedAnswer.description: You usually cannot confirm that safely from appearance alone. Review framing above and below the wall, roof and floor load paths, foundation support, and concealed utilities; structural plans or calculations may be needed. Have the wall assessed before demolition, especially in a multistory or remodeled home.
